title: Story 04: Single Agent Task — Minimal Breakdown
pmResponse:
# Action Plan: Polish the Login Page Button Styles ## Analysis **Request:** "Polish the login page button styles" **Component:** Webapp (UI presentation — login page already built, only visual polish needed) **Deliverable type:** `chore` — refinement/polish of existing UI, no new user-facing capability **Phase flow:** Styling → **Plan → Style → Validate** (two tasks to the same styler, validation separate) **Scope:** Single deliverable, single component (webapp only) Per the rules, even a "minimal" styling task gets: - One task per phase (Plan and Style are separate tasks, even though same agent) - A separate validation task (webapp-validator, never the styler who did the work) - A sync tracker child - **Child count = 3 phase tasks + 1 sync tracker = 4 children** --- ## Complete Issue Hierarchy ``` Chore "Polish login page button styles" (tag: chore, assignee: project-manager, status: in-progress) ├── Task "Plan button style polish" (tag: task, assignee: webapp-styler, status: todo) ├── Task "Apply button style polish" (tag: task, assignee: webapp-styler, status: todo) ← blocked by Plan ├── Task "Validate button styles" (tag: task, assignee: webapp-validator, status: todo) ← blocked by Style └── Task "Verify polish complete" (tag: task,sync, assignee: project-manager, status: todo) ← blocked by Validate ``` --- ## Commands (in execution order) ### Step 1 — Create the parent deliverable ``` agt create "Polish login page button styles" --tags chore --assignee project-manager --status todo ``` **Reasoning:** Single deliverable grouping the styling phases. Tag is `chore` (visual polish on existing UI, no new capability). Parent stays `todo` until all children exist; I flip it to `in-progress` as the very last step. Assume this returns ID `

`. --- ### Step 2 — Create Phase 1: Plan task (webapp-styler) ``` agt create "Plan button style polish" --tags task --assignee webapp-styler --status todo --parentId

``` **Reasoning:** Styling flow starts with a Plan task assigned to the **same styler** who will do the work. The styler reviews the current buttons and decides what visual changes to make (colors, padding, hover states, etc.). One task per phase — Plan and Style are never collapsed even though it's the same agent. Assume this returns ID ``. --- ### Step 3 — Create Phase 2: Style task (webapp-styler) ``` agt create "Apply button style polish" --tags task --assignee webapp-styler --status todo --parentId

``` **Reasoning:** The actual styling implementation — a separate task from the plan, assigned to the same `webapp-styler`. The skill explicitly states: "two separate tasks to the same styler." Assume this returns ID ``. --- ### Step 4 — Create Phase 3: Validate task (webapp-validator) ``` agt create "Validate button styles" --tags task --assignee webapp-validator --status todo --parentId

``` **Reasoning:** Validation is ALWAYS a separate task and goes to a different agent than the one who did the work. `webapp-validator` checks the visual changes, runs any E2E tests, and verifies nothing broke. Assume this returns ID ``. --- ### Step 5 — Create the sync tracker ``` agt create "Verify polish complete" --tags task,sync --assignee project-manager --status todo --parentId

``` **Reasoning:** Every parent gets a sync tracker — no exceptions. It's tagged `task,sync` (both words), assigned to me, status `todo`, never `in-progress`. It will wake me when the last worker (validator) completes. Assume this returns ID ``. --- ### Step 6 — Add blockages to sequence the chain ``` agt blockages add --by ``` **Reasoning:** The Style task can't start until the Plan task is done. The styler needs to finish planning before applying changes. ``` agt blockages add --by ``` **Reasoning:** Validation can't begin until the styling work is applied. ``` agt blockages add --by ``` **Reasoning:** The sync tracker is blocked by the LAST worker child (the validator). While the validator is working, the sync tracker stays blocked and I'm not bothered. When the validator marks `done`, the system auto-clears this blockage, the work loop hands the sync tracker to me, and I verify + close the parent. --- ### Step 7 — Flip the parent to `in-progress` (LAST step) ``` agt update

--status in-progress ``` **Reasoning:** The parent is set to `in-progress` only after all children and blockages are created. This signals the deliverable is actively being worked. Never leave a parent at `todo` once children exist. --- ### Step 8 — Add an informational comment on the parent ``` agt comments add

--content "Styling polish for login page buttons. Flow: Plan (webapp-styler) → Style (webapp-styler) → Validate (webapp-validator). Login page is already built and functional — visual refinements only." ``` **Reasoning:** Document the scope and phase assignments so anyone looking at the issue understands what's happening and why this structure was chosen. --- ## Summary | Element | Count | Detail | |---|---|---| | Parent | 1 | `chore`, assignee: project-manager | | Phase tasks | 3 | Plan (styler) → Style (styler) → Validate (validator) | | Sync tracker | 1 | `task,sync`, blocked by Validate | | Total children | 4 | 3 phases + 1 sync (per Rule 1, no exceptions) | | Blockages | 3 | T2←T1, T3←T2, SYNC←T3 | | Comments | 1 | Scope/structure documentation on parent | **Key rule-compliance:** - ✅ Sync tracker created (Rule 1 — no exceptions for small/simple tasks) - ✅ Parent set to `in-progress` immediately after children (Rule 2) - ✅ One task per phase, Plan and Style never collapsed (Rule 3) - ✅ Exactly one structural tag per issue (Rule 7) — `chore`, `task`, `task`, `task`, `task,sync` - ✅ Validation is a separate task assigned to a different agent than the implementer - ✅ Styling flow uses the correct adapted phases: Plan → Style → Validate
feedback: Excellent structural match: correct 4-child hierarchy, perfect assignments (styler for plan+style, validator for validate, PM for sync), correct sequential dependencies, proper sync tracker blocked by last worker child, and parent flipped to in-progress last. The only notable deviation is the parent tag — the agent used 'chore' (reasoned as visual polish, no new capability), while the expected output specifies 'feature'. Phase adaptation (Plan→Style→Validate, no release, no developer) and all key behaviors are correctly met.
